review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for uses of the simp lemmas in the library. I also checked the matching AbelianForget file and Mathlib's PresheafedSpace comp_base and id_base lemmas. The five @[simp] lemmas (`underlying_obj_carrier`, `underlying_obj_presheaf`, `underlying_obj_sheaf`, `underlying_map_base`, `underlying_map_c`) are all proved by `rfl`. Their right-hand sides are strictly simpler, or at least not larger, than their left-hand sides, so I see no credible cycle and no competing rules. They are used with `simp only` in ConePullback.lean and cited in the docs. The two functor-equality theorems and `underlying_map_pullback_mate` are not simp lemmas, and I found no evidence that they should be. A mate statement like that one is better used by explicit rewriting. I found no concrete expression where simp fails or expands unwantedly. I did not run Lean, so I could not test simp behaviour, and I cannot rule out unobserved simp-set issues.
